meta.title: The US State You Can Only Drive To From Canada
meta._convention: Duration omitted per beat -- build_video.js fills it in from measured narration length. highlight stays ['US'] throughout (the Angle is US territory); Canada/Manitoba/Ontario are carried by markers, matching the Kaliningrad-script convention of only highlighting the country the video is about.

beats.voText: This is the only part of the US mainland north of the 49th parallel, and you can't drive there without leaving the country.
It's called the Northwest Angle, a remote pocket of Minnesota stranded above the border by an inaccurate 1783 treaty map.
Treaty negotiators assumed the Mississippi's headwaters sat near here. They didn't, and by the time surveyors found the mistake, the border was already law.
Today, the only land route in cuts straight through Manitoba, Canada, drive south again, and you're back in the United States.
beats.onScreenText: Drive through Canada to get home.

beats.voText: There's no border agent. Locals use an honor-system phone booth to call in and self-report when they cross back into the US.
One inaccurate line on a 1783 map, and Americans still cross an international border twice just to reach their own state. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
